speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
text: asked the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment regarding the recent record-breaking hawker stall rent exceeding $10,000 per month (a) whether this signifies a trend of escalating hawker stall rentals; and (b) what impact will such a trend have on food affordability and accessibility for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Tenderers submit bids based on various business considerations, such as client profiles, the footfall of the location, expected patronage, and operating hours.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: So, there is no pressure for people to bid higher if they feel that the characteristic of the place does not warrant such high price.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Overall, this is a very popular centre as it is open for three meals throughout the day and has good footfall, especially given the recent opening of a new MRT station and additional developments that are near this centre.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: While a few stalls at popular locations have attracted high bids, I must explain that such high tender prices are not the norm.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Nonetheless, NEA has various measures in place to moderate hawker stall rents.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: Besides not setting a reserve rent for tenders and disallowing subletting, tendered rents are also adjusted after the first tenancy term of three years towards an assessed market rent determined through independent professional valuation.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Sustainability and the Environment (Dr Koh Poh Koon) (for the Minister for Sustainability and the Environment)
text: NEA will continue to monitor hawker stall rentals closely.

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: While the focus has been on food affordability for consumers, how does the Ministry assess the impact of increasing hawker stall rentals on small business owners and aspiring new entrants into the hawker trade?

speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng (Yio Chu Kang)
text: And what are the kind of support that are given to these groups amidst these rental increases?

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As far as the stall rental pressures are concerned, NEA does provide hawkers with a conducive environment, including ensuring that rentals are kept reasonable and affordable at hawker centres.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, for example, NEA has put in place a series of measures to ensure that the rentals in our hawker centres are fair and not speculative.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: As I mentioned in my reply earlier, this includes disallowing subletting or assignment of hawker stores to prevent stallholders from engaging in rent-seeking behaviour.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, they basically just pass on the higher rent to the next guy who wants to sublet from them –and that is something that we disallow.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Also, NEA measures include adopting a transparent and fair monthly tender exercise, as I mentioned.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Since March 2012, the reserve rent has therefore been removed in the tender of vacant stores to allow stall rentals to reflect fully the market conditions based on what people tendered.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For the remaining over 6,000 stallholders, they are paying rent no higher than assessed market rent.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: In fact, for some of our new hawker centres, under the Socially Conscious Enterprise Hawker Centre management model, NEA will take into consideration tender proposals holistically, including the total cost that hawkers will bear before we award the tender to the operator.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: And thereafter, the successful tenderer is required to maintain the same rates for charges collected from stallholders throughout the tenancy term.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, there is more cost certainty to many of the stall operators.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: Since September 2019, operators of new hawker centres are also required to stagger their stall rentals for the first two years of the centre's operations at 80% and 90% respectively, before stallholders pay the full rental costs in the third year.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, this is to help stallholders manage their operating costs as they gradually establish a clientele in that hawker centre over the first two years of their operation.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: For those who have, for example, bid a very high price, such as $10,000 or $8,000, in their first tenancy term, this price will hold.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: But following their first tenancy term, that price will be adjusted to the assessed market rent, which is about $1,800 to $1,500, thereabout.

speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
text: So, that will help to make the price more sustainable for this hawker in the longer term over the next tenancy terms.
